private_note: Cedar gives us 76, but delegates 2, 4, 7, 8 and 11 all said they'd rather keep today than adopt it. That's five firm no votes, so Cedar can't reach nine. Alder keeps us at 72 and adds an income floor and health coverage, which is real insurance for a teacher and an apprentice. It's the only plan we can realistically get that doesn't cost us. I'm moving my first choice to Alder so it gains momentum. Birch and Hazel still cost us, so I'd rather the convention fail.
statement: I'm moving my first choice to Alder, and I'll say why plainly. Cedar is still better for my household on paper. But five delegates have told us they'll vote for today over Cedar, so Cedar can't reach nine. If we keep voting for it we just end up with today's arrangements. Alder keeps the middle where it is and the fourth fifth nearly so. It lifts the bottom two groups and puts a floor and health coverage under every household, including teachers, tradespeople and the self-employed. Birch and Hazel can't reach nine either; I and others won't accept a cut to the middle. Alder is the one plan that every group except the very top can call a gain, and the top gives up only a few percent. To delegates 3, 6, 9 and 12: we need one or two of you. Alder costs you little, and the alternative is no deal for a generation. I'd ask you to make it Alder.
